notes: Toy configuration for VS3 Task 9 planted fixture BR-FINALTIE-1 (.kiro spec ascension-trials-scalable-two-player-analysis): a game decided only at the final Spellbook tiebreak (REQ-7.3 'a case decided only at the final tiebreak').

One fungible normal domain. Two Trials t1, t2, each reward first=2 (second=0), shared-full ties, local total_power tiebreak, optional allocation. The FINAL result chain is [spell_count, shared]: when the two sides' Recognition-Point totals are equal, the sole first place is decided by the derived-state spell_count statistic, not by Recognition Points.

Acting side A holds fungible=1 with spell_count=5; fixed opponent B holds fungible=1 with spell_count=1 and plays its unit on t1. With one unit A can only ever reach a 2-2 Recognition-Point tie (contest t1 for a shared 2-2, or take the uncontested t2 while B takes t1, again 2-2). On that Recognition-Point tie the final chain compares spell_count: A(5) > B(1), so A takes SOLE first and wins the game -- an outcome produced entirely by the final Spellbook tiebreak. Hand oracle: row win best response +1 (decided at the final spell_count tiebreak on a 2-2 RP tie); row margin best response 0 (A cannot out-score B on Recognition Points with equal budget and shared-full ties). Because an active final Spellbook tiebreak couples the decision, the margin oracle uses the exact exhaustive path (REQ-4.3), while the win oracle models the RP-tie -> A-wins sign directly. Oracle transcribed from the final-result rules (model v2.1 §8.2 spell_count; spec v1.1 §7.9), not reverse-engineered from engine output (REQ-9.4).
